title: A Rebuke to the House of Jacob
summary: The Lord addresses the house of Jacob, rebuking them for claiming the holy city and invoking God while not relying on him.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord addresses the house of Jacob, who are called Israel and have come out of the waters of Judah or baptism.
They swear by the Lord's name and mention the God of Israel, but do not swear in truth or righteousness.
They call themselves of the holy city but do not stay themselves upon the God of Israel, the Lord of Hosts.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The address can be presented as off-screen speech without depicting the Lord or the house of Jacob.
unspecified_visual_details: The identity and appearance of any listeners.
The physical setting of the address.

narration.text: Hearken and hear this, O house of Jacob

doctrinal_or_story_notes: A rebuke and teaching, not a narrated event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the house of Jacob performing a baptism or swearing an oath in a newly staged event.

title: Former Things Declared
summary: The Lord says he declared former things in advance because he knew the people were obstinate and might credit idols for them.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker declared and showed former things from the beginning, suddenly.
The speaker says he did this because he knew the addressee was obstinate.
The speaker declared things before they came to pass so the addressee would not credit an idol or image with them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use off-screen speech; the references to an iron sinew and brass brow are figures of speech, not literal anatomy.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The iron sinew and brass brow are figurative descriptions.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal transformation of a neck or brow.
Do not invent the former things or a visible idol scene.

title: Hidden Things Revealed
summary: The speaker says new, hidden things have been shown and declared, while the addressee did not hear or know them. The speaker says the addressee would deal treacherously.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker says the addressee has seen and heard all this, asks whether they will declare it, and says new, hidden things have been shown that the addressee did not know.
The speaker says the things were created now, not from the beginning, and declared before the addressee heard them, lest the addressee claim prior knowledge.
The speaker says the addressee did not hear or know, that their ear was not opened, and that the speaker knew they would deal treacherously; they were called a transgressor from the womb.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The words may be presented without visibly depicting the speaker or addressee.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker's and addressee's identities and appearances.
The hidden things and the setting.

narration.text: And that I have showed thee new things from this time, even hidden things, and thou didst not know them.
They are created now, and not from the beginning,
even before the day when thou heardest them not they were declared unto thee,
for I knew that thou wouldst deal very treacherously, and wast called a transgressor from the womb.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses address an addressee; neither identity is supplied.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict specific hidden things or events.
Do not invent identities, appearances, a setting, or additional speech.

title: Refined in Affliction
summary: The Lord says he will defer his anger and not cut the people off, and that he has refined and chosen them in affliction.

explicit_facts.text: For his name's sake, the speaker will defer anger and refrain from cutting the addressee off.
The speaker says he has refined and chosen the addressee in the furnace of affliction.
The speaker will not suffer his name to be polluted or give his glory to another.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The furnace of affliction is figurative; use off-screen speech rather than a literal furnace.
unspecified_visual_details: The identity and appearance of the addressee.

narration.text: I have chosen thee in the furnace of affliction.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The furnace language is a figure of speech.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the addressee inside a literal furnace.

title: The First and the Last
summary: The Lord calls Jacob and Israel to hearken, declares himself the first and the last, and speaks of laying earth's foundation and spanning the heavens.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord calls Jacob and Israel to hearken and says, "I am the first, and I am also the last."
The Lord says his hand laid the foundation of the earth and his right hand spanned the heavens.
The Lord calls to the heavens and they stand up together.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The heavens may be shown as a setting, but no divine appearance is described.
unspecified_visual_details: The visual form of the heavens standing up.

narration.text: I am the first, and I am also the last.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage is divine speech; no appearance of the Lord is specified.
prohibited_inventions: Do not give the Lord a physical appearance or depict creation details beyond the stated imagery.

title: The Lord's Word and Babylon
summary: The Lord calls the listeners to assemble and hear, declaring that he will fulfill his word and act upon Babylon and the Chaldeans.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord calls all to assemble and hear, and says the Lord has loved him and will fulfill his word.
The Lord says he will do his pleasure on Babylon and his arm shall come upon the Chaldeans.
The Lord says he has called him to declare, brought him, and he shall make his way prosperous.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use off-screen speech; Babylon and the Chaldeans need not be shown as present.
unspecified_visual_details: The identity of "him" in the passage.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage is a declaration and teaching, not a narrated battle or arrival.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the identity or appearance of "him" or depict an attack on Babylon.

title: Come Near and Hear
summary: The Lord says he has spoken openly from the beginning and that the Lord God and his Spirit sent him; the Redeemer says the Lord teaches and leads Israel.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker invites the audience to come near and says he has not spoken in secret.
The speaker says the Lord God and his Spirit have sent him.
The Lord, Redeemer and Holy One of Israel, says the Lord God teaches and leads the people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Render the teaching as off-screen speech, with no speaker depicted.
unspecified_visual_details: The identities and appearances of the speakers referred to as "me" and "him."
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses contain divine speech and references to the Lord and his Spirit, but do not describe a visible appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an undescribed divine figure or identify the unnamed speaker.

title: The Peace They Might Have Had
summary: The Lord laments that had Israel hearkened, its peace would have been like a river and its righteousness like the sea's waves; its seed would have been numerous.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says that if the people had hearkened to his commandments, their peace would have been as a river and righteousness as the waves of the sea.
Their seed would have been as sand, and their offspring like gravel; their name would not have been cut off or destroyed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use the river, waves, and sand as figurative comparisons within the off-screen teaching.
unspecified_visual_details: The people being addressed and the setting.

narration.text: then had thy peace been as a river

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are conditional comparisons, not narrated events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a literal transformation of the people into sand or gravel.

title: A Call to Leave Babylon
summary: The Lord commands the people to leave Babylon and flee the Chaldeans, declaring in song that the Lord has redeemed his servant Jacob.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord tells the people to go forth from Babylon and flee the Chaldeans.
They are told to declare with singing to the end of the earth that the Lord has redeemed his servant Jacob.

reasonable_visual_inferences: This is a command within the teaching; do not stage an actual departure as occurring now.
unspecified_visual_details: The people addressed, their appearance, and the setting.

narration.text: The Lord hath redeemed his servant Jacob.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse issues a command and declaration; it does not narrate the people's departure.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a present-tense exodus from Babylon.

title: Water from the Rock
summary: The Lord recalls that he led the people through deserts, caused water to flow from a rock, and split the rock so the waters gushed out.

explicit_facts.text: The people thirsted not as he led them through the deserts.
He caused waters to flow out of the rock, cleaved the rock, and the waters gushed out.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The recalled event may be shown as a distinct past moment in the desert, with water flowing from a split rock.
unspecified_visual_details: The people's identities, number, and appearance.
The desert's precise location and appearance.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: This verse explicitly recounts a past physical event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the people or add a visible divine figure.

title: No Peace for the Wicked
summary: The Lord declares that despite all he has done, there is no peace for the wicked.

explicit_facts.text: Despite all this and greater things, the Lord says there is no peace unto the wicked.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Present the declaration as off-screen speech rather than depicting a new event.

narration.text: there is no peace, saith the Lord, unto the wicked.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse states a teaching, not a visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a scene of punishment or identify particular people as wicked.
